title: What If Earth Stopped Orbiting and Fell Into the Sun?

scenes.text: What if Earth stopped moving around the Sun? You would have about sixty-five days left.
Earth races sideways at thirty kilometers a second. Stop that, and the Sun's gravity pulls it straight in.
By day forty-one, Earth crosses the orbit of Venus. By day fifty-seven, it crosses Mercury's.
Heat builds slowly, then fast. Roughly fifty degrees Celsius after a month, a hundred twenty-five by day fifty.
On the final day, calculations put the temperature near three thousand degrees Celsius.
Earth never hits the Sun because it keeps missing it. Sideways speed is the only thing holding us up.

description:
What if Earth stopped moving around the Sun?
It would fall straight in, crossing Venus's orbit on day 41 and Mercury's on day 57, and be gone in about 65 days.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Would you rather the Sun fell toward us or us toward it? What should we run through next?
